content.text: No audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right against Client exists anywhere in the Agreement — the only documentation mechanic runs in our favour.

input.quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4), provided that Client timely pays all contested amounts.
input.rationale: Searches for audit, inspection, verification, records, books, monitoring, on-site and premises language returned no right for TrueLink to audit, inspect or verify Client's usage, records or systems. The compensation mechanics (§ 5(a), invoicing on a flat monthly/schedule basis) and the Client covenants (§ 8) contain no records-examination or reverse-audit right, and § 6 runs the other way — it gives Client, not TrueLink, a documentation and charge-contest right. The only TrueLink access-type rights are technical anti-spam mechanisms within its own Interface (§ 8(f)) and Client's Y2K-remediation access obligation (§ 9), neither of which is a usage audit. With no audit right binding Client, the outcome exceeds the preferred position (nothing to limit as to frequency, notice, auditor independence, cost allocation or system access), so no redline is warranted; adding an audit clause would only create a Vendor right we do not currently face. Result is better than preferred, not merely at the fallback.
